He spent the latter part of his life in France, having been summoned to the court of Louis XI. He was canonized in 1519 and is venerated as the patron saint of Calabria and of Italian seafarers.

The Sanctuary of Saint Francis of Paola stands inland from the historic centre, in a ravine associated with the saint’s early religious life. The complex includes an older basilica, a convent and a modern church built to accommodate larger congregations. It is a major pilgrimage destination in Calabria, particularly during the annual celebrations in early May. In the historic centre, the church of the Annunziata and the fountain known as the Fontana dei Sette Canali are among the town’s landmarks.

Paola is also a railway junction. Its station lies on the main Tyrrhenian line between Battipaglia and Reggio Calabria and serves as the coastal terminus of the line to Cosenza. The inland route crosses the Coastal Range through the Santomarco tunnel, linking the town to the provincial capital on the other side of the mountains.

Li Baoyu was born in 703 into a family of Central Asian origin that had settled in the Liangzhou region, around present-day Wuwei in Gansu. His family had long been associated with horse breeding and military service. His great-grandfather, An Xinggui, had helped bring Liangzhou under Tang rule in 619 by overthrowing Li Gui, a rival of the dynasty’s founder, Emperor Gaozu. Li Baoyu was originally named An Chongzhang and later took the given name Baoyu. In 757, during the rebellion begun by An Lushan, he asked to relinquish the surname An because he did not wish to share it with the rebel leader. Emperor Suzong granted him the imperial surname Li.

Li served under the Tang commander Li Guangbi during the rebellion. In 759, when the rebel ruler Shi Siming advanced on Luoyang, Li Guangbi withdrew his forces to Heyang, a strategic position on the Yellow River. Li Baoyu was entrusted with defending one of the fortified positions there. He held it against Shi Siming’s forces, helping prevent the rebels from dislodging the Tang army from Heyang. His service during the rebellion led to appointments as a military governor.

Under Emperor Daizong, Li’s responsibilities shifted to the western approaches to the capital, Chang’an. He held command at Fengxiang, in present-day Shaanxi, at a time when the Tibetan Empire was pressing into Tang territory. The danger to the capital became especially clear in 763, when Tibetan forces briefly occupied Chang’an and Daizong was forced to flee. Li remained in senior military command on the western frontier in the years that followed. He died in 777 and received the posthumous name Zhaowu; he is consequently known by the full title Duke Zhaowu of Liang.

The Swallows of Kabul is a novel by the Algerian writer Mohammed Moulessehoul, published under the pen name Yasmina Khadra. It first appeared in French in 2002 as Les Hirondelles de Kaboul. John Cullen’s English translation was published in 2004. Set in Kabul under Taliban rule, the novel follows two married couples whose lives intersect after a public stoning.

Mohsen Ramat and his wife, Zunaira, once expected to pursue professional careers. Zunaira, a former lawyer, rarely leaves home rather than submit to the restrictions imposed on women in public. Early in the novel, Mohsen joins a crowd stoning a woman accused of adultery. He later tells Zunaira what he did, and his confession strains their marriage. On a subsequent outing, Taliban patrolmen humiliate the couple. When they quarrel at home, Zunaira pushes Mohsen, who falls and dies. She is arrested and sentenced to death.

Zunaira is placed in the custody of Atiq Shaukat, a prison guard whose wife, Musarrat, is terminally ill. Atiq becomes infatuated with Zunaira and wants to save her. Musarrat offers to take the condemned woman’s place, using the anonymity of the burqa to conceal the substitution. The exchange allows Zunaira to escape, but she does not return to Atiq. Desperate to find her, he tries to lift the veils of women in the street and is set upon by a crowd.

The novel draws a contrast between the anonymity of public punishment and the intimacy of the decisions that bring the two couples together. The veil, which Zunaira resents as a restriction on her public life, also makes Musarrat’s act of substitution possible. An animated film adaptation, directed by Zabou Breitman and Éléa Gobbé-Mévellec, premiered in the Un Certain Regard section of the Cannes Film Festival in 2019.

Forrest grew up in Augusta, Georgia, and emerged as one of the leading American amateur boxers in the light welterweight division. He won a silver medal at the 1991 World Amateur Boxing Championships, losing to Kostya Tszyu in the final. After defeating Shane Mosley at the United States Olympic trials, he represented his country at the 1992 Summer Olympics in Barcelona, where he lost his opening bout to Peter Richardson of Great Britain. He turned professional later that year.

Known as “the Viper,” Forrest used his height, reach, and accurate jab to control bouts at a distance. He won the vacant International Boxing Federation welterweight title in May 2001 by outpointing Raúl Frank in a rematch; their first meeting had ended in a no contest following an accidental clash of heads. In January 2002, Forrest challenged the previously unbeaten Mosley for the World Boxing Council welterweight title. He knocked Mosley down twice in the second round and won by unanimous decision. Forrest also won their rematch that July, but lost the title in January 2003 when Ricardo Mayorga stopped him in the third round. Mayorga won their second bout by majority decision.

After a layoff during which he underwent shoulder surgery, Forrest returned to competition in 2005 and moved up to light middleweight. He defeated Carlos Baldomir in 2007 to win the vacant WBC title in that division. Sergio Mora took the title from him by majority decision in June 2008, but Forrest regained it by unanimous decision in September. The rematch was his final bout, leaving him with a professional record of 41 wins, three losses, and one no contest.

Outside boxing, Forrest helped establish Destiny’s Child, an Atlanta organization that provided residential services for people with developmental disabilities. He was fatally shot during a robbery in Atlanta on July 25, 2009, at the age of 38.

On May 21, 1941, the American freighter *Robin Moor* was intercepted in the tropical Atlantic by the German submarine *U-69*, commanded by Jost Metzler. The ship was sailing from New York to ports in southern Africa, carrying commercial cargo that included automobiles and steel rails. The United States was still neutral in the European war, and the freighter’s American registry was confirmed when the submarine stopped it. Metzler nevertheless ordered the ship abandoned, maintaining that its cargo could be used by Britain and its allies. The crew and passengers took to four lifeboats before the submarine sank the freighter with a torpedo and gunfire.

All 46 people aboard survived, although the lifeboats became separated and their occupants spent days at sea before they were picked up. Eleven survivors were rescued by the Brazilian freighter *Osório* after 18 days and taken to Recife, Brazil. A British vessel rescued the other 35 and brought them to Cape Town, South Africa. The separate rescues meant that the fate of those in the other boats was not immediately known when the first survivors reached land.

The sinking drew a formal protest from the United States. In a message to Congress on June 20, President Franklin D. Roosevelt described it as “an act of intimidation” intended to influence American policy. He rejected the idea that Germany could determine where American merchant ships might sail and argued that putting the passengers and crew into small boats far from land had endangered their lives, even though all had survived. The incident did not bring the United States into the war, but it sharpened a dispute already under way over neutral shipping and freedom of navigation. In the months before the American declaration of war in December 1941, encounters between German submarines and American vessels continued to increase tensions in the Atlantic.

After graduating in physical and chemical sciences from the University of Lisbon, Valadares continued his training abroad with support from Portugal’s Junta de Educação Nacional. At the Radium Institute in Paris, he worked under Marie Curie and completed a doctorate in 1933. His research concerned X-ray spectroscopy, in which the characteristic wavelengths emitted by a material can be used to identify the elements it contains. On returning to Lisbon, he taught in the university’s Faculty of Sciences and helped establish a programme of experimental research in atomic and nuclear physics at a time when Portuguese universities had few facilities for such work.

Valadares also applied X-ray methods to the examination of paintings. He collaborated with João Couto at the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga in Lisbon, where radiography allowed researchers to look beneath the visible surface of a painting without removing paint. The resulting images could reveal differences in the materials used, earlier compositions, and changes made during or after the painting’s execution. This work helped establish technical examination as part of the museum’s study and conservation of its collections.

In 1947, Valadares was among a number of university teachers and researchers dismissed by the government of António de Oliveira Salazar. The dismissals disrupted the research group he had helped build in Lisbon and ended his teaching career at the university. He returned to France and joined the Centre national de la recherche scientifique, where he continued his work in experimental physics. He remained in France for the rest of his career and died in Paris in 1982. His career linked the development of experimental physics in Portugal with the French laboratories in which he trained and later worked, while his collaboration with Couto extended the use of laboratory methods beyond the university and into the museum.

Sandaime J Soul Brothers is a Japanese dance and vocal group formed in 2010 under the management of LDH. Its name, meaning “third-generation J Soul Brothers,” reflects its place in a lineage that began in 1999. The original J Soul Brothers became Exile in 2001, and a second generation was formed in 2007. When the members of that lineup joined Exile in 2009, the J Soul Brothers name was revived for a new group.

The third-generation lineup consists of vocalists Ryuji Imaichi and Hiroomi Tosaka and performers Naoto, Naoki Kobayashi, Elly, Kenjiro Yamashita, and Takanori Iwata. Naoto and Kobayashi, who had both belonged to the previous generation, became co-leaders of the new group. Imaichi and Tosaka were selected through the 2010 Vocal Battle Audition 2. The group released its debut single, “Best Friend’s Girl,” in November 2010 and its first studio album, J Soul Brothers, in June 2011.

The group’s recordings draw on pop, R&B, hip-hop, and electronic dance music. Its 2014 single “R.Y.U.S.E.I.” marked a commercial breakthrough, and the running man step in its choreography became closely associated with the song. “R.Y.U.S.E.I.” won the grand prize at the 56th Japan Record Awards, and “Unfair World” earned the group the same award the following year. The 2015 studio album Planet Seven, which included “R.Y.U.S.E.I.,” reached number one on the Oricon weekly album chart.

As part of the Exile Tribe collective, the group has appeared in concerts and other projects alongside related acts while maintaining its own recording and touring schedule. Its members have also worked independently: Imaichi and Tosaka have pursued solo recording careers, while Iwata has appeared in films and television dramas. In 2023, the group released the single “Stars” and embarked on a Japanese arena tour of the same name.

Napoleon Zervas was born in Arta on 17 May 1891. He enlisted in the Greek army in 1910 and fought in the Balkan Wars. During the National Schism, which divided Greece over its participation in the First World War, he sided with Eleftherios Venizelos against King Constantine I. He subsequently served in the army of the Venizelist provisional government. His military career remained bound up with republican politics during the interwar years, when rival factions of officers repeatedly intervened in Greek political life.

After the Axis occupation of Greece in 1941, Zervas helped establish the National Republican Greek League (EDES). He organized its armed wing in Epirus, where it became one of the principal guerrilla forces in occupied Greece. In November 1942, his fighters joined guerrillas of the Greek People’s Liberation Army (ELAS) and British Special Operations Executive personnel in destroying the railway viaduct at Gorgopotamos. The operation was a rare instance of cooperation between the two major resistance armies. By autumn 1943, EDES and ELAS were fighting each other as well as the occupation forces. A truce in February 1944 halted their clashes temporarily, but renewed fighting after the German withdrawal forced Zervas and his troops to evacuate to Corfu in December.

Zervas’s wartime record remains controversial because of the role of EDES forces in the expulsion of Muslim Cham Albanians from Epirus in 1944 and 1945. Although some members of the Cham community had collaborated with the occupation authorities, the expulsions affected the wider Muslim Cham population and were accompanied by killings of civilians.

After the war, Zervas founded the National Party of Greece and entered parliament in the 1946 elections. He served as minister of public order in 1947, during the Greek Civil War, and later joined the Liberal Party. He died in Athens on 10 December 1957.

In anthropology, a chiefdom is a form of political organization in which several communities are linked under the authority of a chief. Unlike a village head whose influence may depend largely on persuasion and personal reputation, a chief typically occupies a recognized office that endures beyond the tenure of any individual. Succession is often restricted to members of a particular lineage, although inheritance need not follow a fixed rule. Rival claimants may draw support from different branches of a ruling family, and a chief’s practical authority can depend on maintaining alliances with local leaders.

The distinction between a chiefdom and a state is not always clear. In one influential classification developed in the twentieth century, the chiefdom occupied a position between relatively autonomous communities and states with more specialized administrative institutions. Some researchers distinguished between simple chiefdoms, in which local communities answered directly to a paramount chief, and complex chiefdoms, in which subordinate chiefs formed an additional tier of authority. Such categories are now often treated as descriptive rather than as stages through which all societies must pass. Political authority can expand or fragment over time, and neighboring societies with similar populations may organize power in quite different ways.

Chiefs have often exercised authority through a combination of ritual leadership and control over resources. A chief might receive food, labor, or valuable goods from constituent communities and use part of that wealth to support feasts, reward followers, or sponsor public works. Archaeologists investigating societies without written records look for evidence such as differences in settlement size, monuments that required coordinated labor, and unequal distributions of burial goods. None of these features establishes the existence of a chiefdom on its own: monumental construction, for example, can also be organized by communities without hereditary leaders. The interpretation therefore depends on how several lines of evidence fit together.

Studio 666 is a 2022 American horror comedy film directed by B. J. McDonnell from a screenplay by Jeff Buhler and Rebecca Hughes, based on a story by Dave Grohl. The members of Foo Fighters—Grohl, Taylor Hawkins, Nate Mendel, Pat Smear, Chris Shiflett, and Rami Jaffee—play fictionalized versions of themselves. The supporting cast includes Whitney Cummings, Leslie Grossman, Will Forte, and Jeff Garlin, with cameo appearances by Lionel Richie and horror filmmaker John Carpenter.

In the film, the band moves into an Encino mansion to record its tenth studio album. Grohl struggles with writer’s block until he discovers a tape left by Dream Widow, a metal band whose recording sessions in the house ended in a massacre. The tape contains an unfinished composition that Grohl begins developing with his bandmates. As the sessions continue, he falls under a demonic influence and becomes obsessed with completing the piece, while the other musicians begin to uncover the history of the house.

The film grew out of Foo Fighters’ sessions for their tenth album, Medicine at Midnight, which was recorded in the same Encino house used as the film’s principal location. The production drew on the contrast between the band’s public camaraderie and the conventions of supernatural horror and slasher films. Grohl also recorded music under the name Dream Widow, extending the fictional band beyond the film. A self-titled Dream Widow EP was released on March 25, 2022.

Open Road Films released Studio 666 in American theaters on February 25, 2022. It received mixed reviews, with critics generally more receptive to the practical gore effects and the band’s willingness to make fun of itself than to the film’s pacing and running time. It was released less than a month before Hawkins’s death.

The Details is a 2011 American black comedy written and directed by Jacob Aaron Estes. It stars Tobey Maguire and Elizabeth Banks as Jeff and Nealy Lang, a married couple living in suburban Seattle. Laura Linney plays their eccentric neighbor, Lila, while Kerry Washington and Ray Liotta appear as Rebecca and Peter, another married couple drawn into the Langs’ troubles. Dennis Haysbert plays Lincoln, a friend of Jeff’s. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2011 and was released theatrically in the United States by the Weinstein Company in November 2012.

Jeff, a physician, discovers that raccoons have been tearing up his newly laid lawn in search of grubs. His attempts to get rid of the animals create trouble with Lila, but the escalating problems in his household have less to do with the raccoons than with his efforts to conceal his own behavior. Already frustrated by the lack of intimacy in his marriage, Jeff sleeps with his friend Rebecca. Her husband, Peter, discovers the affair and confronts him. Meanwhile, Jeff’s friendship with Lincoln presents him with a chance to help someone in need, a subplot that complicates the distinction between his generosity and his desire to see himself as a good person.

The story is told largely in flashback, with Jeff recounting the events that led to the crisis in his marriage. His narration places the initial emphasis on the raccoons, treating their arrival as the start of a chain of misfortunes, while the events themselves repeatedly show how his decisions make matters worse. The film combines the everyday concerns of home improvement, marriage, and relations between neighbors with increasingly serious consequences. Its humor stems in part from the contrast between the relatively minor problem that opens the story and the elaborate deceptions Jeff comes to regard as necessary to preserve his domestic life.

Volumes formed in Los Angeles in 2009 and became associated with the djent movement within progressive metalcore. The band’s early music combined low-tuned guitars and syncopated riffs with atmospheric passages, while vocalists Michael Barr and Gus Farias alternated screamed vocals with more melodic delivery. After releasing the EP The Concept of Dreaming in 2010, the group issued its debut album, Via, through Mediaskare Records in 2011. Its second album, No Sleep, followed on the same label in 2014. Both records paired the rhythmic complexity of the band’s early material with clean vocal passages.

Barr left the group in 2015 and was replaced by Myke Terry, formerly of Bury Your Dead. Volumes subsequently signed with Fearless Records, which released Different Animals in 2017. The album was the band’s first with Terry and made greater use of melodic choruses and hip-hop influences. The track “On Her Mind” featured rapper Pouya, while “Left for Dead” retained the heavier guitar sound of the group’s earlier releases. The band followed Different Animals with the EP Coming Clean in 2019.

Gus Farias departed in late 2019, and his brother, guitarist and founding member Diego Farias, left the band in early 2020. Diego died in February of that year. Barr returned in 2020, joining Terry as co-vocalist alongside bassist Raad Soudani and drummer Nick Ursich. The band marked Barr’s return with the single “holywater,” its first release to feature both Barr and Terry. That lineup went on to record Happier?, released through Fearless in November 2021. On the album, the two vocalists used both harsh and clean delivery, rather than dividing those roles between them. Songs such as “Bend” emphasized melodic singing, while “FBX” placed greater emphasis on the low-register riffs and rhythmic accents that had characterized the band’s earlier work.

Dolphin Tale 2 is a 2014 American family drama written and directed by Charles Martin Smith. A sequel to Dolphin Tale (2011), it returns to the Clearwater Marine Aquarium in Florida, where a rescued bottlenose dolphin named Winter lives with a prosthetic tail. Winter and Hope, another dolphin rescued by the aquarium, appear as themselves. Nathan Gamble and Cozi Zuehlsdorff reprise their roles as Sawyer Nelson and Hazel Haskett, alongside Harry Connick Jr., Ashley Judd, Kris Kristofferson, and Morgan Freeman.

Several years after the events of the first film, Winter’s elderly companion, Panama, dies. Winter becomes withdrawn, and the aquarium must find her another companion to comply with federal rules requiring that dolphins be housed with others of their kind. Sawyer and Hazel hope that Mandy, a recently rescued dolphin, can stay with Winter, but Mandy recovers well enough to be released into the wild. Her release leaves the staff facing the possibility that Winter will have to be transferred to another facility. Meanwhile, Sawyer must decide whether to leave Clearwater to take part in a marine science program.

The arrival of Hope, an orphaned young dolphin, gives the aquarium another chance to keep Winter. Their first introduction goes poorly: Hope is unsettled by Winter’s missing tail and unusual movements. The staff try again with Winter wearing her prosthesis, and the two dolphins begin swimming together. With Winter no longer alone, Sawyer decides to take the opportunity to study away from home.

Although the film dramatizes the circumstances under which the dolphins met, Hope’s rescue was a real event. She was found in Florida waters in December 2010, five years after Winter’s rescue. The closing credits include footage of the dolphins and the aquarium’s rescue work. Warner Bros. released the film in the United States on September 12, 2014.

Hazbin Hotel is an American adult animated musical comedy series created by Vivienne Medrano. It follows Charlie Morningstar, the princess of Hell, as she opens a hotel where sinners can attempt to redeem themselves and earn a place in Heaven. Charlie sees rehabilitation as an alternative to the annual extermination in which angels descend into Hell to reduce its population. Her girlfriend, Vaggie, helps manage the hotel, while its first resident, the adult-film performer Angel Dust, becomes the first test of her proposal. The hotel also receives help from Alastor, a powerful demon known as the Radio Demon, who offers his services for his own amusement rather than out of faith in Charlie’s plan.

The series originated as an independently produced pilot released on YouTube on October 28, 2019. The pilot was financed in part through Medrano’s Patreon and introduced the hotel and its principal characters. A24 subsequently picked up the project for development as a television series. The first season premiered on Amazon Prime Video on January 18, 2024, and ran for eight episodes. Several roles were recast between the pilot and the series, with Erika Henningsen taking over as Charlie, Stephanie Beatriz as Vaggie, and Amir Talai as Alastor.

The television series incorporates original songs by Sam Haft and Andrew Underberg into its episodes. The musical numbers range from Broadway-style ensemble pieces to pop and rock songs, with lyrics that often reveal motives the characters leave unstated in dialogue. In “Loser, Baby,” for example, the bartender Husk challenges Angel Dust’s public persona by admitting to his own failures. The hotel’s experiment also gives the series a way to explore the rules of its fictional afterlife: although its characters are assigned to Heaven or Hell, neither realm’s authorities can clearly explain what would allow a soul to move from one to the other.

In synchronization applications, holdover is the operating state in which a clock continues to supply timing after its reference becomes unavailable or is judged unreliable. While locked to a reference, the clock estimates the frequency correction needed to keep its local oscillator aligned. On entering holdover, it uses the last valid correction or a prediction based on measurements made before the interruption. This distinguishes holdover from free-running operation, in which the clock does not use such previously acquired information.

A clock can enter holdover without a sudden change in its output phase, but any residual frequency error causes its time to drift relative to the reference. A constant fractional frequency error of one part per billion, for example, produces about 3.6 microseconds of time error in an hour. In practice, the frequency error can change as the oscillator ages or its temperature varies. Holdover performance therefore depends on the stability of the oscillator, the quality of the estimate made before reference loss, and the environmental conditions during the interruption. Some clocks use temperature measurements or an aging model to update their frequency correction while the reference is absent.

Holdover is used in telecommunications networks, broadcast systems, and other installations that depend on a common frequency or time base. An interruption may result from the loss of a satellite timing signal or from failures or excessive delay variation along a packet-based timing path. The useful holdover interval depends on the application: a system that needs only frequency alignment may continue operating after the accumulated time error has exceeded the limit for an application that requires events to occur at nearly the same instant. When a valid reference returns, the clock compares it with its local output and may correct the offset gradually, rather than stepping the output time and disrupting equipment that relies on a continuous clock.

Manchester United began their Premier League campaign with a 3–1 home defeat to Crystal Palace and lost 6–1 to Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford two weeks later. Their results improved in November, and a 1–0 victory away to Burnley in January took them to the top of the table. United equalled the Premier League record for the largest winning margin when they beat Southampton 9–0 at Old Trafford on 2 February. They eventually finished second with 74 points, 12 behind champions Manchester City. United went unbeaten away from home in the league, winning 12 matches and drawing seven.

In the Champions League, United opened the group stage with a 2–1 win away to Paris Saint-Germain and a 5–0 home victory over RB Leipzig. However, they lost three of their remaining four matches, including a 3–2 defeat in Leipzig in the final group fixture. United finished third and transferred to the Europa League, where they eliminated Real Sociedad, AC Milan and Granada before defeating Roma 8–5 on aggregate in the semi-finals.

United faced Villarreal in the Europa League final in Gdańsk on 26 May. Gerard Moreno put the Spanish side ahead in the first half, and Edinson Cavani equalised ten minutes after half-time. The match remained level at 1–1 after extra time, and the first 21 penalties in the shoot-out were all converted. Villarreal goalkeeper Gerónimo Rulli scored his own kick and then saved David de Gea’s attempt to give his side an 11–10 victory.

United also reached the semi-finals of the League Cup, where they lost 2–0 at home to Manchester City, and the quarter-finals of the FA Cup, where they were beaten 3–1 by eventual winners Leicester City. Bruno Fernandes was United’s leading scorer in both the Premier League, with 18 goals, and all competitions, with 28.

iAUDIO was a brand of portable digital audio players produced by Cowon, a South Korean consumer electronics company. The brand debuted in 2000 with the iAUDIO CW100, a flash-memory MP3 player. Cowon subsequently introduced both compact flash-based players and larger models with hard drives. Although the name was closely associated with music playback, some models also offered FM radio, voice recording, and playback of photographs or video.

The design of the controls varied considerably across the range. The hard-drive-based iAUDIO M3 had no screen on the player itself, relying instead on a display built into its wired remote control. This allowed users to browse tracks while leaving the main unit in a pocket or bag. The later iAUDIO X5 placed a color screen and a small joystick on the player itself and added photo and video playback. Cowon also experimented with miniature hard drives: the iAUDIO 6 used a 0.85-inch drive, while its successor, the iAUDIO 7, retained a similar compact design but switched to flash memory.

Support for audio formats was a distinguishing feature of the line. In addition to MP3 and Windows Media Audio, various models could play Ogg Vorbis and FLAC files, although compatibility depended on the model and firmware version. Cowon marketed its sound adjustments under the JetEffect name. These settings combined an equalizer with optional effects, including BBE processing and bass enhancement, and could be changed independently of the audio files.

Many iAUDIO players appeared on a computer as USB mass-storage devices, allowing users to copy music directly without a dedicated synchronization application. Cowon nevertheless distributed its JetAudio software with some models for playback and file conversion on a computer. On models that browsed music by folder, the directory structure copied to the device also determined how albums and tracks were organized on the player.

Alexander Gordon (1752–1799) was a Scottish physician whose study of an outbreak of puerperal fever in Aberdeen provided early evidence that the disease could be carried from one patient to another by doctors and midwives. Born at Milton of Drum in Aberdeenshire, he studied at Marischal College and served as a surgeon in the Royal Navy. After further training in midwifery in London, he returned to Aberdeen in 1785 and became physician to the Aberdeen Dispensary.

Between 1789 and 1792, Gordon recorded 77 cases of puerperal fever, 28 of them fatal. In his 1795 work, *A Treatise on the Epidemic Puerperal Fever of Aberdeen*, he presented a table of cases that named the attendants. He found that successive cases were often linked by a midwife, nurse or physician who had attended an earlier patient. The pattern was so consistent that he said he could sometimes predict which women would fall ill from knowing who was to attend them. He acknowledged that he himself had carried the infection to a number of women. He also noted that the outbreak coincided with an epidemic of erysipelas and argued that the two diseases were related.

Gordon advised that clothing and bedding used by patients should be burned or purified, and that attendants should wash themselves and fumigate their clothes before attending another delivery. His recommendations for treating women who had already fallen ill were less sound: he advocated early and substantial bloodletting, a practice then widely used for inflammatory diseases. The lasting importance of his treatise lay in the evidence it assembled for transmission by attendants, decades before Oliver Wendell Holmes and Ignaz Semmelweis made their better-known arguments about the spread of puerperal fever. Gordon returned to naval service in 1795 and died of tuberculosis in 1799.

The episode shifts attention from Glenn Quagmire, usually a supporting character on *Family Guy*, to his sister Brenda and her relationship with her boyfriend, Jeff. Brenda comes to Quahog after Glenn is hospitalized, and Jeff accompanies her. What begins as a family visit becomes a source of concern for Glenn and his friends as Jeff insults and physically assaults Brenda. She minimizes his behavior and defends him when others question how he treats her. The episode uses these exchanges to show the difference between what the people around Brenda can see and what she is willing to acknowledge in front of them.

Lois Griffin tries to persuade Brenda that she does not have to remain with Jeff. The family and friends eventually hold an intervention, during which Glenn reads a letter recalling the sister he knew before the relationship. The appeal does not have the effect he hopes for: Brenda announces that she is pregnant and that she and Jeff intend to marry. Glenn, Peter Griffin, and Joe Swanson then decide to kill Jeff. They take him on a hunting trip, where a confrontation ends with Glenn killing him. Brenda is subsequently led to believe that Jeff has left her.

The depiction of domestic abuse marked a departure from the series’ usual reliance on episodic conflicts and comic reversals. Glenn’s letter, in particular, gives him an extended dramatic scene that draws little on the sexual humor normally associated with the character. The episode nevertheless retains jokes and exaggerated violence, and the combination drew criticism from reviewers who found the shifts in tone jarring. The ending also leaves a tension unresolved: although the intervention asks Brenda to recognize the abuse and make a decision about her future, the resolution comes through a decision made by the men without her knowledge.

Insufflation is the introduction of a gas, powder, or vapor into a body cavity or passage. In modern medicine, the term most often refers to the controlled delivery of gas to create space for an examination or an operation. In laparoscopy, for example, carbon dioxide is introduced into the abdominal cavity to lift the abdominal wall away from the organs. The resulting space, known as a pneumoperitoneum, allows a surgeon to see and manipulate tissues without making a large incision. Carbon dioxide is commonly used because it does not support combustion and is readily absorbed into the bloodstream and exhaled through the lungs.

Insufflation also aids examination of the digestive tract. During endoscopy, air or carbon dioxide can be introduced to expand the lumen and separate folds that might otherwise conceal parts of the lining. Carbon dioxide is absorbed more rapidly than the main components of room air and can therefore reduce bloating and discomfort after a procedure. In computed tomographic colonography, gas is used to distend the colon so that its inner surface can be assessed on reconstructed images. The appropriate degree of distension depends on the procedure: too little can obscure structures, while too much can cause discomfort or injury. In laparoscopic surgery, elevated abdominal pressure can also affect breathing and circulation.

The term can refer to the delivery of powders as well as gases. Nasal insufflation deposits a powdered substance on the nasal lining, where it may act locally or be absorbed into the bloodstream. In respiratory medicine, the term appears in mechanical insufflation–exsufflation, a method of assisting a weak cough. A device first delivers air under positive pressure to expand the lungs, then rapidly switches to negative pressure. The resulting outward flow helps move secretions toward the mouth, where they can be expelled or removed.

The Phelps and Gorham Purchase grew out of competing claims by New York and Massachusetts to lands in what is now western New York. In the Treaty of Hartford of 1786, Massachusetts recognized New York’s sovereignty over the disputed territory but retained the right of preemption, the exclusive right to purchase the land from its Indigenous owners. In 1788, Massachusetts agreed to sell that right to a syndicate led by Oliver Phelps and Nathaniel Gorham. The agreement covered about six million acres and called for payment of one million dollars in Massachusetts securities, in three installments. It did not itself extinguish Indigenous title.

Phelps negotiated with representatives of the Six Nations at Buffalo Creek in July 1788. The agreement reached there covered about 2.25 million acres, most of it between the preemption line on the east and the Genesee River on the west. It also included a tract extending west of the river near its falls, where Phelps intended to establish a mill. The proprietors had the acquired land surveyed into townships and opened a land office at Canandaigua, from which they sold parcels to settlers and other investors.

The syndicate did not complete the original purchase. An increase in the value of the Massachusetts securities made the remaining installments more costly than anticipated, and Phelps and Gorham surrendered their preemption rights to the lands they had not acquired from the Six Nations. In 1790 they sold much of their remaining property in the eastern tract to Robert Morris, who subsequently resold it to a group of British investors associated with Sir William Pulteney. Morris also acquired the preemption rights to much of the western territory directly from Massachusetts. Indigenous title to most of that western land remained in place until the Treaty of Big Tree in 1797, under which the Seneca ceded a large tract while reserving several parcels.

“Dealbreakers Talk Show No. 0001” is the seventh episode of the fourth season of the American television comedy series 30 Rock. Written by Kay Cannon and directed by Don Scardino, it originally aired on NBC on December 3, 2009. The episode follows Liz Lemon (Tina Fey) as she steps away from her job as head writer of TGS with Tracy Jordan to host a talk show based on her relationship advice book, Dealbreakers. The book grew out of a catchphrase from a TGS sketch and had already made Liz recognizable outside the writers’ room.

Jack Donaghy (Alec Baldwin) produces the talk show, but the production runs into trouble before Liz can interview a guest. Asked to perform simple gestures for the opening titles, she becomes increasingly self-conscious in front of the camera. The difficulty is compounded by Jack’s concern that a failed show will give his rival, Devon Banks, an opening to undermine him. Meanwhile, Frank Rossitano (Judah Friedlander) takes over as head writer of TGS. The demands of managing the staff soon lead him to adopt some of the habits and mannerisms for which he and his colleagues had mocked Liz.

In a separate storyline, Tracy Jordan (Tracy Morgan) wants to have a daughter with his wife, Angie (Sherri Shepherd). He decides to demonstrate his ability to commit to a long-term goal by winning an Emmy, a Grammy, an Oscar, and a Tony, a combination known as an EGOT. Whoopi Goldberg, who had already won all four awards, appears as herself and discusses the distinction with Tracy. Although Liz’s talk show does not go forward, Tracy’s pursuit of the four awards continues beyond the episode, providing a recurring storyline during the remainder of the season.

A thyristor-switched capacitor (TSC) is a shunt branch used in alternating-current power systems to supply capacitive reactive power. It consists of a capacitor bank in series with a thyristor valve and a small reactor. The valve contains thyristors connected in inverse parallel, allowing current to flow in either direction when the appropriate devices are fired. The reactor limits the rate of rise of current at turn-on and helps limit the transient current that can result from switching. Several branches may be installed in a static VAR compensator, where they are switched independently to vary the total reactive power in discrete steps.

When a branch is taken out of service, the control system stops sending firing pulses, and the conducting thyristors turn off at the next natural current zero. The capacitor retains a charge because the open valve interrupts its normal discharge path. As the supply voltage continues to alternate, the voltage across the valve is the difference between the instantaneous supply voltage and the voltage retained by the capacitor. To minimize the switching transient when the branch is reconnected, the control system normally waits until this difference is zero or as small as possible. If the retained capacitor voltage exceeds the peak supply voltage, the smallest difference occurs at the supply voltage crest of the same polarity.

Unlike a thyristor-controlled reactor, a TSC is not normally regulated by varying the firing angle during each half-cycle. Once connected, the branch remains in conduction on successive half-cycles and supplies reactive power that varies approximately with the square of the bus voltage at a fixed frequency. In compensators that contain both types of branch, the capacitors provide steps of capacitive output while the reactor absorbs a continuously adjustable amount of reactive power, smoothing the overall response between steps.

Organised Australian rules football took hold on the Gold Coast in the early 1960s with the formation of a local league. Southport, established in 1961, became one of the competition’s leading clubs. It won nine local premierships before joining the Queensland Australian Football League in 1983, where it won the premiership in its first season. The move gave a Gold Coast club a regular place in Queensland’s premier competition.

The Gold Coast first hosted a national-league club in 1987, when the Brisbane Bears entered the Victorian Football League, later renamed the Australian Football League (AFL). Despite their name, the Bears played their home games at Carrara Stadium. Crowds were often small, and in 1993 the club moved its home games to the Gabba in Brisbane. Carrara later returned to the AFL fixture as a venue for occasional matches, including North Melbourne home games in 2007 and 2008. North Melbourne rejected an AFL proposal to relocate permanently, and the league proceeded with plans for a new Gold Coast club.

The new club fielded a team in Victoria’s under-18 TAC Cup in 2009 and in the Victorian Football League in 2010 before entering the AFL as the Gold Coast Suns in 2011. The Suns recorded their first AFL win against Port Adelaide at Football Park in Adelaide and played their first match at the redeveloped Carrara Stadium against Geelong in May. They added a team in the AFL Women’s competition in 2020.

Southport continued to compete in Queensland and regional leagues after the Suns entered the AFL. In 2021 the Sharks joined the expanded Victorian Football League, which by then included clubs from Queensland and New South Wales. They reached the grand final in 2022, losing to the Casey Demons.

Divided by Night is the fourth studio album by the American electronic music duo the Crystal Method, comprising Ken Jordan and Scott Kirkland. It was released on May 12, 2009, through the duo’s Tiny E Records label. It was their first studio album in five years, following Legion of Boom in 2004. In the intervening years, the duo had composed music for the film London and released Drive, a continuous mix originally commissioned by Nike for its series of running workouts.

The album alternates between instrumentals and tracks built around guest performances. The opening title track and “Double Down Under” use the breakbeats and layered synthesizers associated with the duo’s earlier recordings. Elsewhere, the arrangements vary with the style of the featured performer. Matisyahu contributes vocals to “Drown in the Now,” which was released as the lead single. Emily Haines of Metric sings on “Come Back Clean,” while LMFAO appear on “Sine Language.” The album also features Jason Lytle of Grandaddy on “Slipstream,” Justin Warfield of She Wants Revenge on “Kling to the Wreckage,” and singer-songwriter Meiko on the closing track, “Falling Hard.”

Not all of the collaborations were with vocalists. Peter Hook, the bassist of Joy Division and New Order, plays on “Dirty Thirty” and “Blunts & Robots.” His contributions bring a live bass sound to two tracks otherwise driven by programmed rhythms. The placement of “Falling Hard” after “Blunts & Robots” makes for a marked change in tone at the end of the album, from a bass-heavy instrumental to a softer vocal track.

Divided by Night was nominated for Best Electronic/Dance Album at the 52nd Annual Grammy Awards, held in 2010. It was the Crystal Method’s second nomination in that category, after Legion of Boom. The award went to Lady Gaga’s The Fame.

The West Tyrone by-election was held on 3 May 2018 following the resignation of the constituency's Sinn Féin MP, Barry McElduff. He had been elected at the 2017 general election, succeeding fellow Sinn Féin MP Pat Doherty, who had represented West Tyrone since 2001. The constituency includes Omagh and Strabane and had returned a Sinn Féin candidate at every general election since Doherty first won the seat.

McElduff resigned after posting a video on social media in which he balanced a loaf of Kingsmill bread on his head. The video appeared on the anniversary of the Kingsmill massacre, in which ten Protestant workers were killed in County Armagh in 1976. McElduff said he had not made the connection between the brand name and the massacre and apologised for the offence caused. Sinn Féin suspended him from party duties for three months. On 15 January he announced his resignation, saying that the controversy was causing further grief to the victims' families.

Sinn Féin selected Órfhlaith Begley, a solicitor from Carrickmore, as its candidate. The Democratic Unionist Party stood Thomas Buchanan, a member of the Northern Ireland Assembly for West Tyrone. Daniel McCrossan, who also represented the constituency in the Assembly, stood for the Social Democratic and Labour Party. The other candidates were Chris Smyth for the Ulster Unionist Party and Stephen Donnelly for the Alliance Party.

Begley retained the seat for Sinn Féin with 16,346 votes. Buchanan finished second with 8,390 votes, giving Begley a majority of 7,956, smaller than the majority McElduff had secured at the general election the previous year. Begley was the first woman elected to represent West Tyrone at Westminster. In accordance with Sinn Féin's policy of abstentionism, she did not take her seat in the House of Commons.

Frank Elegar was born in the Bronx, New York, on December 3, 1986. A center who also played power forward, he spent four seasons at Drexel University from 2004 to 2008. He was part of the Drexel team that won 23 games in 2006–07 and earned a berth in the National Invitation Tournament. After going undrafted in the 2008 NBA draft, Elegar began his professional career with Eisbären Bremerhaven in Germany. He subsequently played in Turkey before joining the Estonian club Kalev/Cramo in 2012.

At Kalev/Cramo, Elegar won consecutive Estonian league championships in 2013 and 2014. The club also competed in the VTB United League, where he faced teams from across Eastern Europe. In February 2015 he moved to Olimpia Milano, then known as EA7 Emporio Armani Milano, and played in both the Italian league and the EuroLeague. He later returned to the VTB United League with Enisey Krasnoyarsk and then joined Lokomotiv Kuban for the 2017–18 season. Lokomotiv reached the EuroCup finals that season but lost the best-of-three series to the Turkish club Darüşşafaka.

Elegar went on to play for Tofaş in Turkey and Unicaja Málaga in Spain. With Unicaja, he reached the final of the 2020 Copa del Rey, which the club hosted in Málaga. Real Madrid won the final. Elegar subsequently returned to Italy, playing for Reggiana and Napoli in the country's top division. His career thus included spells in several domestic leagues as well as appearances in both of Europe's leading club competitions.

In international basketball, Elegar represented the United States Virgin Islands rather than the United States. He played for the territorial men's national team in FIBA competition in the Americas, in addition to his club career overseas.
